module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Congruences $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod k$ for hypergeometric values ${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$

a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.

*References:*
- [A278070](https://oeis.org/A278070)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA278070


open Nat Finset

/--
a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (n + 1)).sum fun k =>
    (n.choose k) * ((n + k).pred.choose k) * (k.factorial)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 11 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 106 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 1457 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod{k}$ for all $n$ and $k$. - _Peter Bala_, Mar 12 2023

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/278070.wip.lean#L68"]
theorem a_modeq : ∀ (n k : ℕ), Nat.ModEq k (a (n + k)) (a n) := by
    sorry

end OeisA278070

findings.description: The module title at line 21 calls the function `{}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)`. With two upper parameters and no lower parameters, it is `{}_2F_0`, not `{}_2F_1`. The Lean definition and theorem statements correctly use the intended sequence; only the title is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A278070 defines `a(n) = hypergeometric([n, -n], [], -1)` (read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A278/A278070.seq). DLMF equation 16.2.1 (https://dlmf.nist.gov/16.2#E1) defines the indices p and q as the numbers of upper and lower parameters, respectively.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `{}_2F_1` with `{}_2F_0` in the module title. No mathematical declaration needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The sequence is defined by a finite natural-number binomial sum rather than by OEIS's headline hypergeometric expression.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The hypergeometric summand is (n)_k(-n)_k(-1)^k/k!. Using (n)_k = k!·binomial(n+k−1,k) and (-n)_k = (-1)^k·k!·binomial(n,k) gives exactly the Lean summand. Terms with k>n vanish. At n=k=0, Nat.pred replaces the upper binomial argument −1 by 0, but both zero-th binomial coefficients equal 1, so a(0)=1 is preserved. OEIS also explicitly lists this finite-sum formula. In /workspace/review/equivalence.lean I proved equality with both the terminating Pochhammer sum and its finitely supported infinite series, without sorryAx.

review.notes: All mathematical declarations are faithful: a, a_0 through a_4, and a_modeq. Lean evaluation matched all 371 tabulated OEIS terms. Small congruence instances passed, and modulus zero reduces to reflexivity; I also proved that including modulus zero is equivalent to restricting to positive moduli. OEIS's May 31, 2026 comment records the first conjecture as proved, consistent with research solved and corroborated by arXiv:2608.11941. The exact fork-hosted formal-conjectures proof link was not accessed under the repository-access restriction; the separately hosted OEIS-linked AlphaProof Nexus source has the same definition and theorem statement, but its older proof was not fully revalidated against the current toolchain.
